question: For the Weil-descended decomposition system of Gaudry/Diem index calculus at n = m = 3 over F_{p^3}, does msolve's F4 do a different amount of counted work (total F4 matrix cells) when the system is presented as a merge tree or as the contracted S_4 (monolithic) instead of the chained S_3 system, beyond the spread caused by the choice of separating linear form alone?

claims.text: On every instance all four arms return status ok, the same ideal degree and the same set of verified relations, and that set contains the planted decomposition.
monolithic (contracted S_4) and chain differ in total F4 matrix cells by more than the chain A/A spread, in the same direction at all three primes.
claims.if_supported: a descriptive statement about msolve 0.6.5's F4 on these n = m = 3 toy instances only; no ECDLP cost, scaling, wall-time or other-solver claim
claims.if_not_supported: the presentation effect is within the separating-form spread, or inconsistent across the three primes, for these cells

claims.text: tree and chain differ in total F4 matrix cells by more than the chain A/A spread, in the same direction at all three primes.
Wall time per arm, reported descriptively; it decides nothing (no isolation).

hypotheses.statement: Contracting the internal wire before descent (S_4: 3 unknowns, degree 4 per variable) changes F4's counted work relative to keeping it as 3 extra unknowns (chain: 6 unknowns, degree 2 per variable).
hypotheses.mechanism: The presentations denote the same span (KN-LIT-c9e59d) but give F4 different variable counts, degrees and sparsity; the F4 degree reached and the Macaulay matrix sizes depend on them, not on the solution set.

predictions.minimum_effect: median log2(monolithic/chain) below 0 and beyond the C-aa max |log2 ratio| at every prime

power.note: exact paired sign-flip test on 10 instances per prime: smallest two-sided p is 2/2^10 = 0.00195 < 0.05/6 = 0.00833. The counted metric is deterministic given the form, so one replicate per (arm, instance); between-form variation is the A/A arm. Ten instances resolve only effects consistent in sign across nearly all instances; a mixed-sign effect will read inconclusive.

preflight_runtime.measured_on: pre-freeze dry run on this host (2 vCPU Xeon 2.1 GHz cloud container) at p = 503: msolve 0.03 s (monolithic) to 0.25 s (chain, tree) per call, plus Python system build

primary.name: total F4 matrix cells
primary.unit: matrix entries (rows x columns, dense footprint)
primary.definition: sum over every F4 round msolve prints at -v 2 of rows x columns, summed over every attempt of the execution

secondary.name: total F4 matrix rows
secondary.definition: sum of rows over every F4 round and attempt

secondary.name: maximum F4 degree
secondary.definition: largest deg column in msolve's F4 round table

secondary.name: msolve attempts
secondary.definition: msolve invocations until a non-'failed' status, at most 8

secondary.name: msolve wall time
secondary.definition: subprocess wall time of every msolve attempt (F4, parametrization, output), summed; excludes Python system build and lifting

stopping_rules.rule: fixed design: (30 instances + 1 warmup) x 4 arms = 124 executions, then stop
a row with status other than ok, or missing the planted relation, invalidates its instance for C2/C3 and is reported; the run continues

invalidation_rules: an instance where any arm fails C1 is excluded from every comparison and listed
wall time is descriptive only (isolation none); counted cells stand
msolve 'failed' attempts are retried with a fresh form within the row (max 8) and charged; they are not infrastructure retries

decision_rule.text: For C-mono and C-tree separately: supported_within_scope when, at every prime, the Bonferroni-level (1 - 0.05/6) percentile bootstrap interval of the median per-instance log2(candidate/chain) cells excludes 0, the exact sign-flip p <= 0.05/6, |median| exceeds the C-aa maximum |log2(chain-aa/chain)| at that prime, and the sign is the same at all primes; within_control_distribution when |median| <= that A/A maximum at every prime; invalid_measurement when C1 fails or a prime has no valid instance; inconclusive otherwise.
decision_rule.threshold: CI excludes 0, p <= 0.00833, |median log2 ratio| > A/A max |log2 ratio|, same sign at 3 primes
decision_rule.statistic: median over instances of log2(f4_cells candidate / f4_cells chain), per prime
decision_rule.interval: percentile bootstrap of the median, 20000 resamples, level 1 - 0.05/6
decision_rule.effect_size_measure: median cell ratio 2^median(log2 ratio) per prime

graphs: per-instance log2(candidate/chain) F4 cells by prime with the A/A band

inadmissible: changing primes, instances, forms, flags, metric or the analysis script after seeing data
quoting wall time as a result (isolation none)
reading a supported verdict as an ECDLP cost, scaling, other-solver or other-(n, m) claim
dropping instances other than by the invalidation rules
